programme: NCOR2 (SMRT corepressor, whose target set includes nuclear receptors and the leukemia-fusion gene RUNX1T1) silences differentiation and metabolic-receptor programs; HLF, a PAR-bZIP factor whose targets include EPO, RUNX1, CYP7A1 and the clock genes PER2/DBP, sets a low-turnover, restrained metabolic state; TFAM drives the mitochondrial transcription/biogenesis needed to leave that state; and USF2, an E-box partner whose targets include HBB, PKLR, HOXB4, ABCA1 and ACACA, switches on the associated lineage and lipid-handling genes. Together HLF, NCOR2, TFAM and USF2 read as a corepressor-bZIP-E-box module that toggles progenitor-like cells between a mitochondrially-restrained quiescent state and an actively differentiating/oxidative one.
role_in_a: In cardiovascular disease this kind of module would be expected to govern the metabolic/quiescence state of blood- and vessel-resident progenitor or monocytic cells, and its target genes CYP7A1 and ABCA1 sit directly on cholesterol efflux/bile-acid handling, the core lipid axis of atherosclerotic disease. None of this is documented for the pair here, however — Open Targets records no association for HLF, NCOR2, TFAM or USF2 with Cardiovascular_Disease, so this role is inferred from the target genes, not retrieved.
role_in_b: In sarcoma the same axis has direct, if fragmentary, support: TFAM is implicated in osteosarcoma proliferation/invasion, NCOR2 in MPNST proliferation and in NCOR2-fusion giant cell tumor of bone, and HLF is reported as a broad pan-cancer/tumor prognostic biomarker. This reads as the mitochondrial-biogenesis/corepressor switch being co-opted to sustain proliferative or therapy-resistant tumor states rather than restrained ones.
shared_axis: Both blood/vascular progenitors and mesenchymal soft-tissue progenitors plausibly rely on an NCOR2/HLF/TFAM/USF2-driven switch between a mitochondrially-quiet, self-renewing state and an actively proliferating/differentiating one; a shared vulnerability in that switch could let both vascular or monocytic cells in cardiovascular disease and stromal cells in sarcoma escape normal restraint. No retrieved source states this connection for the pair — it follows from the common developmental/metabolic logic of the factors' target genes, not from documented cross-disease work.
reasoning: The four factors form a nameable module (corepressor + PAR-bZIP + mitochondrial biogenesis + E-box) and three of the four (HLF, NCOR2, TFAM) are independently placed in sarcoma by the retrieved literature, satisfying 'some factors placed' in one disease. But nothing places any of them in cardiovascular disease (Open Targets is blank for all twelve factors in CVD), and no source discusses the module as a unit or connects it across the two diseases, so the account rests on reasoning about shared cell-state biology rather than retrieved evidence — the definition of moderate, not strong.
support: 39145052 — HLF pan-cancer bioinformatics analysis, places HLF in tumor biology broadly; 38711550 — HLF as prognostic/immunological/therapeutic biomarker across human tumors; 42648418 — HMGA2::NCOR2 fusion drives giant cell tumors of bone/soft tissue; 36497280 — NCOR2 knockdown inhibits MPNST (a sarcoma) proliferation via BDNF/TrkB/ERK; 37300290 — TFAM-targeting compound suppresses osteosarcoma proliferation, migration and invasion. No PMID above addresses USF2 specifically, and none address any of the four factors in cardiovascular disease.
how_to_falsify: In a blood/vascular progenitor line and a sarcoma line already implicated for this axis (e.g. an MPNST or osteosarcoma line), knock down HLF, NCOR2, TFAM and USF2 individually and combinatorially, then measure mitochondrial mass/OXPHOS (TFAM-dependent), quiescence/self-renewal markers, and expression of the shared target genes (CYP7A1, ABCA1, HBB, PKLR, HOXB4, RUNX1T1); if these factors do not co-regulate this gene set as a unit in either cell type — or ChIP/co-binding shows they occupy non-overlapping regulatory regions — the module claim is wrong.
caveats: The blood|soft_tissue tissue pairing most likely reflects the expression data source for each disease's network (blood/PBMC for cardiovascular cohorts, tumor tissue for sarcoma) rather than a shared anatomical site, so it should not itself be read as biological support. Support fractions for the four carrying factors range from 45-54% of the 80 available patient-group comparisons across 6 independent cohort pairs — recurrent but far from unanimous. TBP had comparable recurrence (39/80) but was excluded from the module because, as core Pol II basal machinery with 140 largely non-specific targets, it does not inform a distinct process. Seven other concordant factors (PAX8, CTNNB1, ATF2, E4F1, FOXH1, HBP1, ZMYND8) were left out of the account because they mark unrelated processes (Wnt, TGF-beta/Nodal, stress response, thyroid/renal development, cell-cycle repression) and forcing them in would manufacture a mechanism the data do not support. The tissue-generic exclusion list is dominated by classic blood/immune regulators (SPI1, CEBPB, STAT3, RELB, JUNB) — their removal means the retained module is not simply generic hematopoietic signal, which is some indirect support for its specificity, but the complete absence of any cardiovascular-disease evidence for all twelve factors is the central limitation of this account.
